title: Use semantic color tokens only
rationale: Semantic tokens flip correctly between light and dark and keep brand changes to one file.
body: All color classes must come from the token set in tokens.json (`semanticColorClasses`).

title: No arbitrary Tailwind values
rationale: Arbitrary values bypass the scale, so layouts drift from the system and cannot be changed centrally.
body: Use the Tailwind scale. The only bracket form allowed is a token reference such as `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]`. Variant selectors like `[&_svg]:size-4` are fine because they sit before the utility.

title: No inline styles
rationale: Inline styles skip theming, responsive variants and dark mode.
body: Style only through Tailwind classes and `cn()`.

title: Use design system components, not raw form elements
rationale: The components carry focus rings, invalid states, sizing and accessibility behavior. Raw elements lose all of it.
body: Import the component from `@/components/ui/*`. Check the registry before building a custom one.

title: Only approved imports in route code
rationale: Importing UI primitives or other UI kits directly sidesteps the design system and its decisions.
body: Route code may import React, lucide-react, recharts, the `@/` alias and relative files only.

title: Spacing stays on the scale
rationale: A consistent spacing rhythm is what makes pages read as one system.
body: Padding, margin, gap and size utilities use values from `tokens.json` `spacingScale`.

title: Every form control has an accessible label
rationale: Unlabeled controls fail screen readers and make click targets smaller.
body: Pair each control `id` with a `Label htmlFor`, or give it `aria-label` when a visible label is wrong for the design. Placeholders are not labels.

title: Icon-only buttons need an aria-label
rationale: A button with only an icon has no name for assistive technology.
body: Applies to every Button with a `size` starting with `icon`.

title: No horizontal page overflow at any supported width
rationale: Sideways scrolling on a phone is a broken layout.
dont: fixed widths wider than the viewport
body: Checked at 375, 768 and 1280 px in both themes. Only tables, code and diagrams may be wider, inside their own scroll container.

title: No serious or critical accessibility violations
rationale: Accessibility is a baseline requirement, including color contrast in both themes.
body: axe-core runs in light and dark at desktop width. Serious and critical findings fail the build. Static jsx-a11y rule hits are reported under this record too.

title: Rendered colors resolve to design tokens
rationale: Lint catches class names, but computed styles catch colors that arrive through other paths such as CSS or library defaults.
do: colors that come from --background, --foreground, --primary and friends
body: For text, background and border colors on visible elements, the computed value must match a token color in the active theme (alpha variants allowed).

title: One primary action per view
rationale: Two competing primary actions dilute the main task. The same primary action may appear more than once (e.g. a hero CTA repeated in a footer) — both instances use the default variant because they represent identical intent.
do: use default-variant for the page's primary action
repeat the same default-variant Button for the same action in multiple locations (hero + footer)
use outline or ghost for secondary actions
dont: two default-variant Buttons with different hrefs or different onClick targets on the same page
competing primary actions that ask the user to choose between two destinations
body: Counts distinct primary actions, not distinct primary Button elements. Multiple default-variant Buttons are allowed when they all share the same destination or trigger the same action. Dialog footers may have their own primary.

title: Destructive actions are confirmed with an AlertDialog
rationale: Deleting data without a confirmation step causes irreversible mistakes. Intent is hard to detect from code alone, so the reviewer judges it.
do: Delete button opens AlertDialog with a Cancel and a destructive Action
body: Any control that deletes, removes or resets user data must open an `AlertDialog` that names what will be lost.

title: Pages use the standard layout wrapper and type hierarchy
rationale: A shared page frame and heading scale make pages feel related.
body: See the `page-layout` pattern. The reviewer checks structure and heading order.

title: Pages load without console errors
rationale: Console errors usually point to broken props, missing keys or failed requests.
body: Any `console.error`, page error or failed request during load fails the check.

title: Registry components match approved visual baselines
rationale: Detects the design system itself drifting, such as a token edit or a shadcn upgrade changing every Button.
do: update baselines deliberately with a recorded decision
body: Screenshots of the `/gallery` route in light and dark are compared with committed baselines.

title: Interactive elements must have visible focus indicators
rationale: Keyboard users must be able to see which element has focus. The design system's base styles provide focus rings; route code must not suppress them.
do: Rely on the skin's default focus ring styles
Use Tailwind ring utilities (ring-2, ring-ring) if adding a custom interactive element
dont: opacity-0 on a focus ring class
body:
The Playwright check tabs through visible interactive elements (up to 15) and reports any that have neither a computed outline nor a box-shadow after a keyboard Tab press. This catches `outline: none` overrides that were not paired with a ring replacement.

Focus rings are a skin concern: each skin's CSS sets the base `:focus-visible` style. Do not override them in route code.
